config.title: RTK Query — Data Fetching & Cache

intro.title: RTK Query — Data Fetching & Cache
intro.body:
In this lesson, you will build a simple React app that fetches and displays a list of posts from a mock API. There is no file named “main.” **App.jsx** is the file where you do the work: (1) API service — createApi and endpoints, (2) Redux store — configureStore with the API reducer and middleware, and (3) React UI — Provider and the generated hooks. **store.js** and **api.js** in the file list are optional extras for this lesson; the steps expect your code in **App.jsx** unless you choose to split files yourself.

You will learn how to use RTK Query, a powerful data fetching and caching tool from Redux Toolkit, to manage server state efficiently. The core concepts include setting up an API service, defining endpoints, and using auto-generated hooks to fetch data with built-in loading and error states. By the end, you'll understand how RTK Query simplifies data fetching, reduces boilerplate code, and automatically caches responses to optimize performance.
intro.usecase: RTK Query's data fetching and caching patterns are essential for building responsive dashboards like those in analytics platforms (Google Analytics, Mixpanel) where multiple charts need synchronized data without redundant API calls. E-commerce product listing pages use this pattern to cache search results and filter states while maintaining real-time inventory updates. Social media feeds implement similar caching to instantly display previously loaded posts while fetching new content in the background, creating seamless user experiences.

objectives: Initialize an RTK Query API service with endpoints for fetching and caching data
Configure a Redux store to integrate the RTK Query middleware and reducer
Implement React components that use generated hooks to fetch data from an API
Apply cache management by controlling data refetching and invalidation behaviors
Manulate component state by binding loading and error statuses from query results
Construct a user interface that renders cached data while fetching updates in the background
Integrate mutation endpoints to update server data and automatically refetch related queries

steps.title: Import React from 'react'
steps.instruction: In **App.jsx**, import React from 'react' at the top.
steps.hint: Open App.jsx in the file list and add an import for React at the top.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing React
import React from 'react';
steps.feedbackPartial: Add an import for React from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Import React from 'react' at the top of App.jsx.

steps.title: Import createApi and fetchBaseQuery from RTK Query
steps.instruction: Still in **App.jsx**, import createApi and fetchBaseQuery from '@reduxjs/toolkit/query/react'.
steps.hint: Add an import statement for createApi and fetchBaseQuery from the RTK Query React package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing RTK Query APIs
import { createApi, fetchBaseQuery } from '@reduxjs/toolkit/query/react';

seedCode.App.jsx:
import React from 'react';

// Import createApi and fetchBaseQuery from '@reduxjs/toolkit/query/react' here

steps.expectedOutcome: createApi and fetchBaseQuery are imported from '@reduxjs/toolkit/query/react'.
successCriteria: createApi and fetchBaseQuery are imported from '@reduxjs/toolkit/query/react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've imported the RTK Query APIs.
steps.feedbackPartial: Import both createApi and fetchBaseQuery from '@reduxjs/toolkit/query/react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Add an import for createApi and fetchBaseQuery from '@reduxjs/toolkit/query/react'.

steps.title: Import configureStore from Redux Toolkit
steps.hint: Add an import statement for configureStore from Redux Toolkit.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing configureStore
import { configureStore } from '@reduxjs/toolkit';
steps.feedbackWrong: Add an import for configureStore from '@reduxjs/toolkit'.

steps.title: Create a new API service using createApi
steps.instruction: In **App.jsx**, in the API service section (below your imports), create a new API service using createApi.
steps.hint: Call createApi to create an API service variable (e.g. const api = createApi({}). You will add baseQuery and endpoints in the next step.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating an API service (this step only — config comes next)
const api = createApi({});
steps.expectedOutcome: An API service is created using createApi.
successCriteria: createApi is called to create an API service (e.g. const api = createApi(...)).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the API service with createApi.
steps.feedbackPartial: Call createApi to create your API service variable.
steps.feedbackWrong: Create an API service by calling createApi (you will add baseQuery and endpoints in the next step).

steps.title: Define baseQuery and empty endpoints
steps.instruction: In the API service, define it with a baseQuery using fetchBaseQuery and an empty endpoints object for now.
steps.hint: Pass an object to createApi with baseQuery: fetchBaseQuery({ baseUrl: '...' }) and endpoints: (builder) => ({}).
steps.expectedOutcome: The API service has baseQuery using fetchBaseQuery and an empty endpoints function.
successCriteria: The code includes baseQuery using fetchBaseQuery and an empty endpoints function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've defined baseQuery and empty endpoints.
steps.feedbackWrong: Define baseQuery with fetchBaseQuery and an empty endpoints object.

steps.title: Configure the Redux store
steps.instruction: In **App.jsx**, below the API service, create a Redux store using configureStore from '@reduxjs/toolkit'.
steps.hint: Use configureStore to create a store variable. This is the store setup, not the component.
steps.expectedOutcome: A store variable is created using configureStore.
successCriteria: configureStore is imported from '@reduxjs/toolkit' and used to create a store variable.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've imported configureStore and called it to create a store variable.
steps.feedbackWrong: The store configuration is missing. You need to import configureStore and use it to create a store.

steps.title: Add App and wrap with Provider
steps.instruction:
In **App.jsx**, import **`{ Provider }`** from `'react-redux'` (named import, not default). Define a root **`function App()`** whose **return** value is wrapped in **``** … **``** — put a simple placeholder inside for now (e.g. **`
App
`**). You will add **PostsList** in a later step. End the file with **`export default App`**.
steps.hint: Use `import { Provider } from 'react-redux'`. Build `function App() { return ( <Provider store={store}>...</Provider> ); }` then `export default App`. Your `store` variable should be the one from `configureStore`.
steps.expectedOutcome: Redux store is available via Provider; the module exports a root App component.
successCriteria: A root `App` component returns JSX wrapped in `<Provider store={store}>`.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Use a named import: `import { Provider } from 'react-redux'`. Add `function App()` whose return is wrapped in `<Provider store={store}>`, and `export default App`.
steps.feedbackWrong: You need a real root component: `function App()` (or equivalent) returning `<Provider store={store}>...</Provider>`, plus `export default App`. Do not use `import Provider from 'react-redux'` — Provider is a named export.

steps.title: Generate hooks from the API service
steps.instruction: In **App.jsx**, from your `api` object, export the generated hooks by destructuring (e.g. `export const { useGetPostsQuery } = api;`).
steps.hint: After creating your API service with createApi, you can access auto-generated hooks from the service object. Use destructuring to export them.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: Exporting generated hooks
const { useGetPostsQuery, useAddPostMutation } = postsApi;
steps.expectedOutcome: The generated hooks from your API service are exported and ready to be used in components.
successCriteria: The hooks are exported using destructuring from the API service object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're exporting the hooks using destructuring from your API service object (e.g., `const { useGetPostsQuery } = api;`).
steps.feedbackWrong: The hooks weren't exported correctly. Remember to destructure them from your API service object after creating it with createApi.

steps.title: Create a component to display data
steps.instruction: In **App.jsx**, add a functional component **`PostsList`** that returns a **div** with an **h2** showing **Posts**. Inside **`App`**, replace your placeholder with **`<PostsList />`** (still inside **`<Provider store={store}>`**). Keep **`export default App`** at the bottom — do not switch the default export to PostsList.
steps.hint: Define `function PostsList()` (or `const PostsList = () =>`) with the div + h2. In `App`'s return, nest `<PostsList />` inside Provider. Only `App` is the default export.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a PostsList component that returns a div with an h2 heading.
successCriteria: A functional component named PostsList is defined and returns a div containing an h2 with the text 'Posts'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your component is named exactly 'PostsList' and returns the required JSX structure.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined correctly. Check that you've created a function named PostsList that returns a div with an h2 heading.

steps.title: Use the generated query hook in the component
steps.instruction: In **App.jsx**, inside PostsList, call the auto-generated useGetPostsQuery hook to fetch data and destructure the returned object.
steps.hint: Call the hook (e.g., useGetPostsQuery()) and destructure the result into variables like data, isLoading, error.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: calling a generated hook
const { data, isLoading, error } = useGetPostsQuery();
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now calls the RTK Query hook to initiate data fetching, making the data, loading, and error states available.
successCriteria: The useGetPostsQuery hook is called inside the component
The result is destructured into at least data, isLoading, and error
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're calling the hook and destructuring the result properly. Check the syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: The hook isn't called correctly. Remember to call useGetPostsQuery() and destructure the returned object.

steps.title: Handle loading and error states
steps.instruction: In **App.jsx**, inside PostsList, destructure isLoading, error, and data from the result of the useGetPostsQuery hook call.
steps.hint: The hook returns an object with properties like isLoading, error, and data. Use destructuring assignment to extract them.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: destructuring from a hook result
const { isLoading, error, data } = useSomeQuery();
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have access to isLoading, error, and data variables from the query result.
successCriteria: The useGetPostsQuery hook is called and its result is destructured into isLoading, error, and data variables.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling the useGetPostsQuery hook and destructuring isLoading, error, and data from its result.
steps.feedbackWrong: The destructuring wasn't completed correctly. Check that you're calling the hook and extracting isLoading, error, and data.

steps.title: Display the fetched data
steps.instruction: In **App.jsx**, inside PostsList, map through the data array from the query result and display each post's title in a list item.
steps.hint: Use the data property from the query result. You can use the map method on data to create an array of JSX elements.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will display a list of post titles when the data is successfully fetched.
successCriteria: The PostsList component maps through the data array and renders each post's title in a list item.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the data property from the query result and mapping through it to create list items.
steps.feedbackWrong: The data isn't being displayed correctly. Check that you're accessing the data property and using map to create list items with each post's title.

steps.title: Add a refetch button
steps.instruction: In **App.jsx**, in PostsList, add a button that calls the refetch function from the useGetPostsQuery hook when clicked.
steps.hint: The refetch function is returned by the useGetPostsQuery hook. Add a button with an onClick handler that calls this function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: button that triggers a refetch
<button onClick={() => refetch()}>Refresh Data</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button is added to the PostsList component that will manually trigger a data refetch when clicked.
successCriteria: The button element is present with an onClick handler that calls the refetch function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a button, but make sure it calls the refetch function when clicked.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button is missing or doesn't properly trigger a refetch. Check that you're calling the refetch function from the useGetPostsQuery hook.

steps.title: Implement polling for automatic updates
steps.instruction: In **App.jsx**, configure useGetPostsQuery to refetch every 5 seconds using a pollingInterval option.
steps.hint: Pass an object as the second argument to useGetPostsQuery with a pollingInterval property set to 5000 (milliseconds).
steps.expectedOutcome: The useGetPostsQuery hook will be configured with pollingInterval: 5000 to automatically refetch posts every 5 seconds.
successCriteria: The useGetPostsQuery call includes a second argument object with pollingInterval set to 5000.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're passing the pollingInterval option correctly as the second argument to useGetPostsQuery.
steps.feedbackWrong: The polling configuration isn't quite right. Remember to add pollingInterval: 5000 as an option to the useGetPostsQuery hook.

steps.title: Test the cache behavior
steps.instruction: In **App.jsx**, add a console.log inside PostsList to log data when it's available, so you can observe cache behavior.
steps.hint: Place the console.log after the hook call but before the return statement. Use a conditional to only log when data exists.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will log the fetched posts data to the console when available, allowing you to observe RTK Query's caching behavior when navigating between components.
successCriteria: A console.log statement is added inside the PostsList component that logs the data when it exists.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your console.log is placed after the hook call and only executes when data exists.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've added a console.log statement inside the component that logs the data variable when it's available.
